findings.summary: CP-HI-04 forgets a run's former Primary CTO after takeover
findings.detail: producerSessions selects run/task-scoped assignments and then adds only the run's current owner. PRIMARY_CTO assignments are project-scoped. Call sequence: bind session A as PRIMARY_CTO(P); dispatch run R to A; switch PRIMARY_CTO(P) to B with takeover=true; bind A as BLIND_REVIEWER(R). A's assignment has run_id NULL and R's owner is now B, so assertReviewerIndependence accepts A even though A produced R. Later checks reuse the same incomplete producer set.
findings.suggestedFix: Persist immutable per-run producer membership when ownership or production begins, and base every reviewer-independence decision on that history. A takeover must add the new owner without removing the former owner.

findings.summary: A takeover can repoint runs owned through another role key
findings.detail: The takeover UPDATE identifies runs only by owner_session_id and owner_binding_generation. Generations are scoped per role key, so one session can hold role keys X and Y at generation 1. Switching Y with takeover=true then rewrites a live run owned through X if it has the same session/generation, assigning it to Y's replacement session and role key. The preflight query at line 187 has the same scope error.
findings.suggestedFix: Add owner_role_key = roleKey to both the live-run preflight and takeover UPDATE, and verify that only runs owned by the exact outgoing binding tuple were changed.

findings.summary: revoke can orphan nonterminal runs without a takeover
findings.detail: revoke unconditionally revokes the active assignment and fences its messages without checking whether that binding owns live runs. Call sequence: dispatch R to binding G; call revoke(roleKey); bind a later generation. R remains pinned to revoked G, while owner authorization rejects G because it is no longer active and the new binding does not own R. This bypasses the §11.1 rule that live-owner changes occur only through emergency takeover.
findings.suggestedFix: Refuse revocation while the exact binding owns nonterminal runs, except inside an explicit transactional takeover or suspension path that checkpoints and atomically reassigns or terminates every affected run.

findings.summary: Failover does not fence messages already claimed for delivery
findings.detail: retargetOrReject selects only status='PENDING'. Call sequence: claimDeliverable moves an old-generation message to IN_FLIGHT; switchTo revokes that generation but leaves the row untouched; the transport then sends it and markSent succeeds because it checks only the claim token. If delivery fails instead, markAttemptFailed restores an undeliverable old-generation row to PENDING. Thus an old-generation dispatch can leave after the atomic failover transaction.
findings.suggestedFix: During failover, atomically invalidate old-generation IN_FLIGHT claims as well as PENDING rows. Make markSent and markAttemptFailed conditional on the binding tuple still being current, or on a claim fence version changed by failover.

findings.summary: Delivery and ACK checks do not bind targetSessionId to the active assignment
findings.detail: enqueue accepts an arbitrary target session. claimDeliverable joins the active assignment using only role_key and binding_generation, and acknowledge queries only the current generation. Call sequence: role R generation G is bound to session A; enqueue R/G with target session B; claimDeliverable sends it to B; acknowledge from B/G succeeds because the stored target is B. Session B never held the role, so the fenced envelope does not enforce role isolation.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate the complete active tuple at enqueue, join on a.session_id = o.target_session_id when claiming, and require the ACK session to equal both the envelope target and the active assignment session.

findings.summary: A caller-controlled flag can activate a STARTING session
findings.detail: Both bind and switchTo accept allowStarting=true and treat STARTING as eligible. Call sequence: create an incoming STARTING session; call switchTo with allowStarting=true and takeover=true. The working binding is revoked and messages/runs are moved to a session that has not passed readiness. This contradicts §9.5 and §15.7, which require readiness before binding activation and failover.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove allowStarting from active binding operations and require READY unconditionally. If startup needs pre-registration, represent it separately from an ACTIVE role binding.

findings.summary: Every delivery error is retried without failure classification
findings.detail: markAttemptFailed always returns the message to PENDING. A permanent authentication, invalid-target, or policy error is therefore immediately claimable again, with no failure class, retry eligibility decision, backoff, or terminal attempt limit. This contradicts §34.1, which permits retry only when failure classification and idempotency allow it.
findings.suggestedFix: Accept a typed failure class and retryability decision, terminally reject/escalate non-retryable failures, and apply bounded backoff to eligible retries.

findings.summary: RETARGETED is an unconsumed outbox state
findings.detail: RETARGETED is declared as a status and admitted by the database schema, but no code writes or consumes it. Retargeting deliberately leaves the row PENDING and records OUTBOX_RETARGETED as a reason code. The extra state is an unconsumed schema field/state of the kind §13.3 requires removing.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove RETARGETED from the TypeScript status union and database CHECK constraint; retain the existing reason code if retarget provenance is needed.
